proof:
# An attained bounded-facet alternative for a strict counterexample

Fix a full-rank lattice-convex projection P containing an interior lattice
point z_0, and fix d>=1. Let alpha be any proposed depth threshold. If there
is an actual convex fiber family over P with positive mixed volume and
maximum depth strictly below alpha, then there is an attained minimizer
below alpha in a finite-facet class. It has the following exact alternative:

* It has a zero-volume fiber; deleting all such fibers preserves its measure
  and maximum depth and strictly reduces its lattice-convex projection.
* All its fibers are full-dimensional polytopes, and the fixed-cap volume
  maximality and global support-stress lemma apply within its facet class.

This does not assert that the reduced projection is nonhollow, or that the
stress forces a contradiction. It gives an actual attained object to which
the first-order calculation applies without assuming a general minimizer
is polytopal.

## 1. A strict counterexample has a finite-facet approximation on the same P

For each z choose finite subsets of K_z with convex hulls A_z^l converging
to K_z in Hausdorff distance. Include at least one point in every fiber and
enough affinely independent points in every positive fiber. Let

    C_l=conv union_z ({z} x A_z^l),

and use its ACTUAL fibers K_z^l. Convexity of the original family gives

    A_z^l subset K_z^l subset K_z.

Thus K_z^l converges to K_z, every integer fiber in P stays nonempty, and no
new integer projection point appears. Each C_l is a polytope, so each of its
positive fibers has finitely many facets. Continuity of maximum depth on
fixed finite P, proved in the compactness note, implies that for some l
this polytopal family still has depth below alpha. Let N bound the facet
count of all its positive fibers.

## 2. A closed normalized facet class

Consider all actual families on P with |K_(z_0)|=1 and the following property:
each fiber of positive d-volume has at most N facets; zero-volume fibers are
allowed to be arbitrary nonempty compact convex sets. This class is invariant
under all the normalizations used in
`candidate a14cc5f809b2b766`.

It is closed under the resulting Hausdorff limits. A zero-volume limit is
explicitly allowed. Suppose instead K_l tends to a full-dimensional K and
each K_l has at most N facets. For all sufficiently large l, a fixed ball
B(q,rho) is contained in K_l. Describe K_l by unit-normal facet inequalities

    a_i^l.x<=b_i^l,       i=1,...,k<=N,

passing to a subsequence of constant cardinality k. The bodies are uniformly
bounded, so their touching facet offsets are bounded; take limits of every
normal and offset. All limiting inequalities have slack at least rho at q.
Their intersection Q contains K. Conversely, if y belongs to Q, then
(1-epsilon)y+epsilon q strictly satisfies every limiting inequality and
therefore belongs to K_l for all large l. Hausdorff convergence puts it in K.
Letting epsilon decrease to zero gives y in K. Thus Q=K, which has at most
N facets. This proves closedness at positive-volume limits.

The normalized class is precompact by the fixed-P compactness lemma and
its closure remains in the class. Maximum depth is continuous. It therefore
attains a minimum beta_N, and the approximation of Section 1 ensures
beta_N<alpha.

## 3. The exact alternative

If the minimizing family has zero-volume fibers, use the depth-zero boundary
lemma and positive-projection argument from
`candidate b989614dc4f86228`, Section 5. Removing those fibers
preserves the measure and the maximum depth, and produces the smaller
lattice-convex set P_+ as its exact projection. No comparison between the
full minimizing classes on P and P_+ is asserted.

Otherwise every fiber is a full-dimensional polytope with at most N facets.
The exact full-fiber critical cap cover makes this family a total-volume
maximizer under fixed cap budgets among competitors in the same facet class.
Indeed a larger-volume feasible competitor would have normalized depth
strictly below beta_N and could be normalized centrally back into the class.

For the support-stress argument choose, for EACH fiber, the normal fan of its
small positive inner parallel bodies. Its rays are its original facet
normals; all original facets persist under sufficiently small erosion.
The original support function is linear on this possibly finer fan. Require
support perturbations of that fiber to remain linear on its own chosen fan.
All perturbed fibers therefore still have no facet normals other than its
original ones and have at most N facets. A common refinement provides shared
coordinates; linearity on each individual fan is a finite linear subspace
condition. The exact fiber-compatibility inequalities remain linear there.

This restricted cone contains common erosion, uniform dilation, and every
affine fiber translation/shear used in the stress proof. Every admissible
perturbation stays in the facet class. Consequently all the Farkas stress,
affine moment balances, and the Euler identity in
`candidate 21a9da879344205f` hold for this actually attained minimizer.
